nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of d-NiFeP/CC is 11.4 m^2 g^-1, higher than NiFeP/CC (3.9 m^2 g^-1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: By measuring the nitrogen adsorption–desorption isothermal curves... the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area of d-NiFeP/CC was 11.4 m^2 g^-1 which was higher than that of NiFeP/CC (3.9 m^2 g^-1).

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFeP/CC shows Ni 2p main peak at 853.8 eV (Ni–P), peaks at 857.1 and 875.2 eV; Fe 2p peaks at 712.4, 725.2 eV and 708.1 eV (Fe–P); P 2p peaks at 129.6 (2p3/2), 130.5 (2p1/2) eV (P-M) and 133.9 eV (P–O). Binding energies positively shifted by 0.6-0.8 eV compared to NiFeP/CC, indicating defects and increased metal valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p spectrum, the main peak at 853.8 eV after deconvolution corresponds to Ni–P, and there are also a pair of peaks with binding energies of 857.1 and 875.2 eV... The peaks of Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 are located at 712.4 and 725.2 eV, respectively. In addition, a peak at 708.1 eV... The P 2p spectra of d-NiFeP/CC show three peaks at 129.6, 130.5 and 133.9 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER, d-NiFeP/CC shows polycrystalline disordered NiOOH structure with lattice fringes of 0.208 nm (NiOOH (201)) and FFT diffraction rings of NiOOH (210)/(310).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4a, HR-TEM images confirm that the NiOOH generation from the d-NiFeP/CC pre-catalyst surface reconstruction is a polycrystalline disordered structure... lattice fringes with a plane spacing of 0.208 nm... corresponding to the (201) crystal plane of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: d-NiFeP/CC reconstructs to NiOOH at 1.4 V vs RHE showing Raman peaks at 478 cm^-1 (Eg, δ(Ni-O)) and 578 cm^-1 (A1g, ν(Ni-O)), earlier than NiFeP/CC (1.5 V).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface reconstruction of the d-NiFeP/CC pre-catalyst was monitored by in situ Raman spectroscopy... When the applied potential was increased to 1.4 V; , two Raman peaks appeared at 478 cm^-1 and 578 cm^-1...
